description: This bar chart, titled "PHHEME" and likely from the paper "Bridging Cognition and Emotion Empathy-Driven Multimodal Misinformation Detection," displays the accuracy percentages of different models or configurations on the PHHEME dataset. The vertical y-axis is labeled "Accuracy (%)" and uses a linear scale ranging from 75.0 to 100.0, with tick marks and labels at 2.5-point intervals. The horizontal x-axis lists six distinct categories: "Ours," "w/o comments," "w/o text," "w/o select," "w/o emotion," and "w/o cognition." Each category is represented by a single colored bar with its exact accuracy value labeled on top. The bars are arranged in descending order of accuracy, with the highest value being 90.57% for "Ours" (a dark red bar), followed by 89.62% for "w/o text" (a light blue bar), 87.74% for "w/o cognition" (a dark blue bar), 87.34% for "w/o emotion" (a medium blue bar), 86.82% for "w/o select" (an orange bar), and the lowest value at 80.10% for "w/o comments" (a light yellow bar). The chart visually emphasizes the performance of the "Ours" model as the baseline, showing that removing specific modalities or components (comments, text, selection, emotion, cognition) leads to a measurable decrease in accuracy.
